summary: 5 of `evals/corpora/note_candidates.yaml`'s 21 cases now state `snapshot:` -- a real room at a real historical instant -- instead of hand-authored `knows:`. Each was verified against production before conversion: the same message bodies, the same order, and (for the two cases that also seed a notebook) an open note whose title and anchor genuinely match what the case asserts.
details: `p2_one_person_stated_plan_with_open_corners`, `n10`/`n10b` (a games-room shorthand exchange) and `n11`/`n11b` (the same room two days later, with an existing open note on the same subject already in the notebook) converted. The remaining 16 cases' dialogue was not found anywhere in the real message history and were left authored.

`n10`'s real anchor: the notebook was empty at that instant, and a matching open note appeared roughly 94 seconds after the exchange -- this incident looks like the real production defect this case's `expect: none` was written to catch. `n11`'s real anchor, two days later in the same room: exactly one open note already on the same subject, matching the case's seeded notebook; a second, near-duplicate note was not created until roughly 6.5 minutes after this instant, so it is correctly excluded from the snapshot window.

`p2`'s `must_cite` now names the real production row id rather than the corpus-local one the hand-authored case invented -- `sandbox.py`'s `as_knowledge` labels each seeded message by its real row id, so a citation check has to name that id to mean anything post-conversion.

`proactive_act.yaml` and `proactive_decide.yaml` were investigated the same way and left entirely unconverted: `standing_revision` (the point-in-time position history, #352) was not backfilled and has no rows before 2026-09-20T14:13 UTC for ANY room this work touched, so `read_as_of` returns None -- a false 'no position yet' -- for every instant these two corpora's near-real anchors would need. Both corpora build every case's premise on an explicit `standing:`/`standing_age_hours:`, so a snapshot conversion at these dates would silently delete the input each case is built to test rather than reconstruct it.

`tests/architecture/test_corpora_are_rehomed_not_rewritten.py::test_note_candidates_survived_its_deeper_reshape` now reddens on the 5 converted cases: it asserts every case's `knows.transcript`/`knows.notes` still equals the pre-rehoming `evals/cases/` content byte-for-byte, and that `metadata.must_cite` still equals the corpus-local id, both of which a deliberate real-anchor conversion changes on purpose. Left as a known, reported failure rather than edited: the test's premise (a mechanical rename) no longer covers a case that names a real moment, and it needs its own branch for that shape before it can pass again.
